about: A node's conventions and the lists of readings and tools. Not the protocol: no word reads this file (core.md, section 12). Two nodes that share it can talk.

messages.public_block_about: A message is canonical JSON, whole, and exactly { block, signature }: any other key refuses it (shape). No suite and no version travel beside a block.
messages.proof_about: A signed request carries exactly one of counter (an integer above the highest the node has seen from the signer) or challenge (issued by the node, used once). It carries no time.
messages.pull_answer_about: log is given only when the request names one (nodes.md, Pull); a block with no receipt on that log has no arrival number on it and is not served under it.
messages.push_answer_order: taken and refused: ascending by hash, a block's codes in the order of refusals.codes.block. unjudged and unread: ascending by hash, each needs ascending, each codes in list order. equivocations: each pair sorted, the list sorted. had: ascending by hash.
messages.signature_about: A key signs four shapes, each canonical JSON: a block's header (header, header_optional), a genesis's own bytes, a request without its signature key, an answer without its signature key. A header has hash; a genesis has type; a request has signer and node; an answer has node and neither signer nor hash. A pull answer's request is the bare SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of the whole signed request. header_signature is the block's one signature. An envelope plaintext is the canonical JSON of the plaintext object.
messages.admission_about: per_stranger and strangers_per_day count asks: blocks that name one of the node's people in a ref, never a block's pieces
messages.discovery_about: `reads` lists the rule sets the node runs (core.md, section 11): it lists one only when it runs a build made from that set's files (nodes.md, Discovery).

cbor.about: Compact form of a public block (encoding.md). The id is always the hash of the canonical JSON; CBOR is transport only. `keys` is the key table (keys_about).
cbor.keys_about: The table is made, never edited, by tools/cbor-table.cjs from protocol.json: positions 0 to 9 are type, state, refs, author, prev, seq, at, audience, key, hash; then every other name protocol.json lists for a block's state, refs, terms, scope, a line, a voice, a row, a shape or a kind field, once each, sorted by its UTF-8 bytes. A name a schema adds has no position: it is written as text. A later table appends a new name at the end and never moves or empties one. The table is a convention: a compact-form reader names the table it reads by this file's hash.

bytes.about: A value at one of these paths that matches its grammar is a byte string; otherwise text (an id with a hash prefix stays text). `[]` is each element, `*` any key. hash: 32 bytes. sign_key: std 32 raw bytes (suites.std.sign_key.spki_prefix put back), other suites the whole SPKI. encrypt_key: the suite's raw bytes. nonce: 16 bytes.

cbor.time: A value at a time field (time_fields, in time_fields_checked_in) matching grammar.time is an integer of milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z; when.from and when.to likewise.

message.header_about: A chain header has exactly the four keys. seq is an integer; the three ids are 32-byte byte strings when bare, text when they carry a hash prefix.

peers.about: Three peers: micro, edge, node. A micro that acts and an index are variants.
peers.micro_clockless: a micro may leave out at and when on observe, transform and transfer; its edge writes an observe of kind receipt

profiles.about: Optional. A node that has never heard of a profile still accepts every block in it.

counted_in.input: a ballot result, a commitment, the named counter
counted_in.output: true when the result is signed by that counter and lists the commitment in counted

output.epoch: the current epoch; 0 is the circle actor's key
output.keys: the encryption keys of the epoch's counted rekeys, sorted

residency.regions: plain labels the node's promise and the author's request name, compared by exact equality; the protocol gives none a meaning

folds.about: A reading's fold (folds.md): computed from blocks, read by no word, and changing none of the four answers (core.md, section 10). Each has: ops (the door ops that answer it), over (what it is asked of), input and output.

ways_in.input: a circle and the blocks given

output.rows: [{ row, least }]: a to row its needed, a parts row the fewest owners whose parts reach it (null where none can); never above the every-owner way's
output.every_owner: { least }: the number of ids that own parts; null where there is no every-owner way (no pack, or unissued parts and no meter)

where_now.output: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known

made_from.input: an instance and the blocks given
made_from.output: [{ thing, from, make, took }] sorted by thing then make (folds.md, What each fold returns)

machine_lock.input: a machine (a thing) and the blocks given

output.locked: true when a stop of the machine backed by its owner stands
output.locks: [id], sorted: the standing stops of the machine (grants of kind stop, refs.subject the machine) backed by its owner as the ownership fold reads him in each stop's causal past
output.claimed: [id], sorted: the other standing stops of the machine, each its signer's reading, locking nothing

machine_lock.about: A reading (patterns/machines.md, A machine lock): whether a machine runs is its owner's kit. A lock ends as anything ends, by its author's stop; the lock names no safe state.

use_shown.input: a place, the blocks given, and optionally a named clock (clocks)

output.clock: clocks when a clock was named, else author (each use is dated by its author's own at)
output.users: [{ user, uses, count, unreceived, first, last, seasons, bounds, resting, overlaps, leave }] sorted by user; none means no use in what the reader holds. `leave` is null, or { of, since, until }: the owner's live grant of kind leave to this user for the place, shown as by leave of `of` since `since`, never as a use that stands against the owner

not_free_shown.input: a block and the blocks given

output.shown: [{ block, by, reason, threat, at }] the signer's own words (observe of kind not_free) naming the block in refs.subject, written by the block's author; a claim shown beside the block, never a verdict
output.nothing: [{ block, why }] words by anyone else (why: not_signer): their own observes

invasion_shown.input: a claim of invasion (an observe of kind invasion) and the blocks given

output.holder: who holds the claim now: the claimant, then each accepted hand-over
output.evidence: the claim's derives_from, sorted; empty means evidence: none
output.judges: [{ judge, named_by }] judges named by a message for the claim stating judge, by the holder side or an accused
output.rulings: [{ block, judge, named_by, word, evidence }] a named judge's confirms or defeats of the claim

next_link.seq: the next seq for the key
next_link.prev: the hash of the key's previous block, or of the block that brought the key in

consent.input: a person, a sender (or none), optionally the hash of the grant the sender's block acts under (refs.under), and the blocks given

output.block: the consent block that decides (the lowest hash of tied blocks that agree), or null

consent.about: The person's own blocks count for every word; anyone else's counts only as a stop that binds the recorder's own side, or as a yes that lifts a stop that same recorder recorded and has it in its causal past (consent.md). A stop wins any tie; a tie of other words gives null. There is no public list.

release_shown.input: a deal's first promise or a thing, and the blocks given

output.subject: the block asked about
output.released: [{ block, by, side, to }] counted releases (an observe of kind release) that let go of the signer's own claims on it: one naming it in refs.subject, or, for a deal, a general release by a side to the other side that has it in its causal past and does not list it in state.except; side is from (the price is to come to it) or to (what moves is to come to it), null for a thing; sorted by block
output.kept_open: [{ block, by, side }] general releases that list the deal in state.except: the debt stays open; sorted by block

views.about: A view reads a fold and the reader's clock or arrivals, and says whose.

promise_view.input: a first promise, the blocks given, the reader's clock
promise_view.output: the promise_stage answer, with stage expired once the clock passes expires and nothing binds, and a promise that moves nothing elapsed once the clock passes its terms.until (a fact of its term, never that it was kept; it binds no one); beside the stage, `condition`: holds, not or unread for the offer's terms.condition, null with none; `condition_failed`: when the condition does not hold, the first promise of the deal it names that ended without it (stopped, declined or expired) or that itself rests on one, else null (failure spreads visibly, never just open); `missed`: the dates in force in the order agreed (the first promise's pay_by, then each date both sides signed, in `moved`) that passed before the price was paid in full, or before the reader's clock while it is unpaid; null with no pay_by or on a standing promise

ownership_view.input: an instance, the blocks given, the reader's clock
ownership_view.output: the ownership fold's answer; a transfer that carries a condition counts once the condition holds at the clock given (none given: only a condition that needs no clock)

due.clock: the performer's own, from the anchor's arrival on its node
due.input: a promise with a relative when, the performer's arrivals and clock
due.output: the instant it falls due, or null while the anchor has not arrived

pot.clock: the reader's own, when a payout's condition reads it (none given: only a condition that needs none)
pot.input: a first promise (the head), the blocks given, and the reader's clock (a payout's condition may read it)

output.kind: { unit, of }: the backing's; with none, the one kind every accepted pay-in shares; with a cap of all and neither, the one kind the holder's payouts share; else null, and every sum null
output.backing: a sum, or null when cap is all
output.cap: all when the head's terms.cap is the word all (written out, never a default: all the holder owns on the day a claim is read, the referee fixing the sum; backing and left are then null and a payout is never past the pot), else null
output.paid_in: a sum: accepted pay-ins to_owner the holder
output.held: a sum: payouts that take and have not landed
output.left: backing plus paid_in less held and paid_out; null when cap is all
output.payouts: [{ block, by, to, amount, takes, why, state }]: why also not_confirmed or not_holder

condition_holds.input: a condition, the blocks given, the reader's clock
condition_holds.output: true or false for the shapes the protocol reads (condition_shapes; promises.md, Conditions); null for any other shape (not read)

reading_condition_holds.input: a reading_condition, the blocks given, the reader's clock
reading_condition_holds.output: whether the readings the condition names hold by the reader's clock (patterns/tasks.md)

args: seed: 64 hex (the 32-byte seed of core.md, section 2)

sign.result: signature hex over the block's header as canonical JSON; a genesis: over its own bytes (core.md, section 2: deterministic)

write_refusals.result: core.md, section 8 (a writer signs only what its own read reads): every { code, detail } a writer refuses the draft with, read against the blocks given (a deal block against what it answers, a child grant against its parent), in protocol.json's order; empty when it may be signed. Asked of a draft before anyone signs it.

args: text: a push { messages, for }, its bytes as they arrived (no caller decodes it first)
strict_push.result: { refused, messages } (nodes.md, Push): one list per message, plus one field for a refusal of the whole push. The push's bytes are read first (limits.push_bytes, then limits.read_depth: `size_limit`); then it is the canonical bytes of a strict value whole, exactly { messages, for }, with no float, no null and no whole number past 2^53 - 1 anywhere (`not_canonical`); then no more than limits.push_messages messages (`size_limit`). A push that fails is { refused: { hash, code, detail }, messages: [] }, `hash` the SHA-256 of its bytes. Else { messages }: for each message in order what its block's bytes alone say, as `strict_text` (a sealed message has none)

wrap.result: the message { block, signature } (core.md, section 6): never a suite, never a version

unwrap.result: the full block { hash, type, state, refs, signature }; the id is recomputed, in the suite of the key that signed it (core.md, section 2): with `blocks`, the author's key that opens it; without, the suite the block shows (a genesis's own, else its prev's hash). A message that names a suite is an error (bad_hash); one that carries a version is an error (shape)

args: fixed?: { vectorsOnly: true, ephemeral, contentKey, nonce, keyNonces } (fixed randomness only reproduces a vector; without vectorsOnly: true it is an argument error)
pad?: true pads an object plaintext with `pad` to the next of 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 bytes, then each 4096 (privacy.md, Sealed messages)
seal.result: the envelope (privacy.md); `fixed` gives the random values (hex, the ephemeral private key, content key, content nonce, one key nonce per recipient) so a case is exact; with none the values are random

open.result: the plaintext JSON; a recipient it is not for is an error

cbor_encode.result: lowercase hex of the CBOR message [t, block, signature] (encoding.md); `short` uses key table 1 and t = 1

cbor_decode.result: the full block; the id is recomputed from the canonical JSON, in the suite of the key that signed it (as unwrap). Anything after the signature is an error

passkey_challenge.result: the WebAuthn challenge for the block: base64url, no padding, of the 32 bytes of SHA-256 of its header as canonical JSON; a genesis: of its own bytes (encoding.md, Passkeys)

verify_message.result: true when `signature` opens over the canonical JSON of the object without `signature` (nodes.md)

args: last: full_block of the key's chain, or null
next_link.result: { seq, prev }: the next place in the key's chain (core.md, section 5)

matches.result: true when the block matches the pull filter (nodes.md, Pull)

due.result: the instant it falls due (the anchor's arrival plus `wait`), or null while the anchor has not arrived

promise_views.result: { id: the promise_view answer }: many deals of one store, read against one reading of it

promise_view.result: the same answer, with stage `expired` as folds.md says (a sum is an amount; uncovered { from, to }; unanswered; to_come { to, from, draws }; to_come_on with amount), or { not_shown: true, lacks }

ways_in.result: a reading: { circle, rows: [{ row, least }], every_owner: { least } or null }, or { not_shown, lacks }, or null when the circle is not among the blocks

made_from.result: [{ thing, from, make, took }], sorted by thing then make (folds.md, What each fold returns)

where_now.result: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known (folds.md); a transfer of an amount moves no place

args: clocks?: a named clock, { names, needed } (null dates each use by its author's own at)
use_shown.result: { clock, users } as the fold `use_shown` (folds.md, Uses shown)

not_free_shown.result: { shown, nothing } as the fold `not_free_shown` (folds.md, Words beside a block)

invasion_shown.result: null, or the fold `invasion_shown` (folds.md, A claim of invasion shown)

pot.result: null, or the fold `pot` { holder, kind, backing, paid_in, held, paid_out, left, cap, payouts } (folds.md, A pot), or { not_shown: true, lacks } (folds.md, A chain)

args: under?: grant id the sender's block acts under
admission: { parties?, per_stranger?, order_channel? } as the node's rule states it, or null for no rule; stated, never defaulted

asks_today: integer (stated, never defaulted), the asks this node took today from this block's sender, when it is not in parties: blocks that name one of the node's people in a ref, never a block's pieces (each sender is counted alone)
full_block: a promise with a calendar repeat (state.when a time, state.terms.repeat an RRULE, state.terms.zone)
repeat_occurrences.result: the start times, in UTC and in order, of the occurrences of the promise's calendar repeat from `from` up to but not including `to` (readings/calendar.md): counted from state.when, read in terms.zone by the reader's own release of the IANA time zone database. An error (argument) for a repeat that follows an event, an RSCALE other than GREGORIAN, a part the reader does not read, or a zone not in the reader's release

args: person: a person's or circle's id
backed_all.result: authority.md, Backed by a person: { hash: { backed, why } } for every block of the blocks given, read together once. Each verdict is the one `backed` gives that block among the same blocks

to_come_back.result: promises.md, What is to come back: { to_come: [{ block, amount, to, why }] }, one line for each transfer of the blocks given whose money is the person's by `gives` (signed by them, as their circle, or under a chain of their grants) and that `backed` says they do not back; `why` is backed's sentence. Money their own word or a live chain of their grants backs is not to come back

args: person: a person's or circle's id
gives.result: promises.md, What becomes whose: { gives: [line], bench }, what of the person's would become whose if the block stands, read only from its typed terms and refs. A line is { what | amount, to, back, held }: `held` true where the block is a draw that holds that instance from its signer's word (an offer to a named receiver, or a transfer, naming an instance); `what` a thing, with `amount` when the terms say how much, or `amount` alone (a price, or an amount moved with no instance); `to` the id it becomes the property or use of (null: open); `back` the deal's `terms.until` or null. A promise gives, for its `from` side, each thing it names (each line's `what`, with its quantity chosen, and for a line with no `what` the amount its quantity states; a thing the blocks show another owns is left out) and, for its `to` side, the price (`terms_total`, in any kind); an answer `accepted` reads the promise it answers at the quantities it chooses, any other status gives nothing; a transfer, for the one whose word it is (the circle it is signed `as`, else the principal at the top of its grant's chain, else its author), gives its `state.amount`, and each `refs.what` to `to_owner` as goods, or to `to_holder` as a use that comes back at the `until` of the deal it is `for`. A line to the person herself is left out. No word of a schema or text is read `bench` is the bench of the deal the block belongs to, as promise_stage gives it, or none.

account_of.result: promises.md, Where to pay me: { who, destinations: [{ destination, by }], hash, at } from the head of the account words (observe, kind account) that who signed and that speak for no one else: the one no other of theirs has in its causal past; null when there is none, when two heads do not see each other (nothing fills the choice in), or when the head lists no place (it ends the account). No clock is read

args: block?: the sender's full_block (null for none), so that whom its block speaks for is named too (consent follows the principal)
is_stranger.result: true when the receiver is a stranger to the sender (consent.md): only her accept (a block of hers that binds her and answers one of his accepted), her counter-offer (a promise with no status answering his) or a deal she opened naming him as a side makes him no stranger, and only her own live yes; her declined or stopped answer, any other reply and a recorder's yes do not; the sender is named by itself, its operators and whom its block speaks for

args: text: a code as a person types it
code_matches.result: true when the text names the block: case, spaces and hyphens ignored, O read as 0, I and L as 1; eight characters match the short code, and more characters more of the id, five bits at a time; fewer match nothing

args: at: the block it is read for (its id, or the block)
reading_condition_holds.result: patterns/tasks.md, Sensor conditions: read on the readings in the causal past of the block it is read for, up to that block's own `at` (its signer's word, read against her); never on a reader's clock

args: incoming: [full_block, or sealed message { header, header_signature, envelope? }]

choices: { takes_pairs: boolean, copies?: { signed?, handed_on?, unsigned?, mailboxes? } }, the node's own stated choices (nodes.md, A node's word): with true the blocks of a forked pair arriving together, or forking one it has, are taken as well as listed in equivocations, with false neither is taken; no default. `copies` is its admission rule for sealed copies: `signed` keeps a copy from a signed push by the block's author, `handed_on` one from a signed push by anyone else (never in the author's place), `unsigned` one from an unsigned push, `mailboxes` a wrapped copy ({ mailbox, envelope }) to one of those keys; a rule that states nothing keeps no copy
push?: { signer?, for? }, the push the messages came in
accept.result: { taken: [id], unjudged: [{ hash, needs: [id] }], refused: [{ hash, code, detail }], unread: [{ hash, codes }], equivocations: [[id, id]], false_headers: [id] } in the order nodes.md, Push, fixes. A block whose body the node has, or a header that describes a body it has, is nothing new and is listed nowhere; a block that waits only on a suite needs [] With `copies` or `push` given, it adds copies: [{ hash, for, from }] (from: author or handed_on), sorted by hash, and wrapped: [{ mailbox, bytes }], what it keeps of each wrapped copy (which mailbox, how big after padding; not who wrote it).

args: log: [{ n, block, header?, header_signature?, copies? }]: each block with its arrival number n (at least 1) on the log the request names, or the node's own number when it names none; an entry with no such n has no arrival number there and is never served

choices: { cap: integer of at least 1, serves_pairs: boolean }, the node's own stated choices (nodes.md, A node's promise): the most blocks one answer carries (a pull's limit is cut to it), and whether the other half of a forked pair is sent with an answer that includes one; no default
through?: the last arrival number the node read to answer, or null
answer_pull.result: { node, request, log?, blocks: [{ n, message }], next, signature } (nodes.md, Pull); `log` only when the request names one; `signature` only when a private key is given; an answer that is not full has `next` at least `through`

spec.result: { protocol, rule_set }: the contents of protocol.json, and the id of the rule set this build is made from (core.md, section 11), or null where the build was given no manifest

merkle_root.result: encoding.md, Large content: the Merkle root (64 hex) over the chunks; an error (argument) for no chunks

merkle_proof.result: the proof of that chunk: the sibling hashes (hex) from the leaf up; an error (argument) for an index that is no chunk

merkle_verify.result: true when the block's `state.marks` holds exactly one `{ scheme: "merkle", value }` mark, `state.chunks` (its signed count) is an integer of at least 1, and the proof shows the chunk is chunk `index` of that many under that root; the count is never an argument

args: fence?: a grant's state.fence, or null (it fences nothing and lets no time alone)
at: the time asked about (the protocol reads no clock)
readings?: null or { name: amount }, what the machine's sensors last signed
heard?: the time of the newest block the machine has heard from its node, or null
fence_reading.result: patterns/machines.md, A machine's fence: { within, why, alone, alone_until }. within: true when no reason is listed. why: [{ code, of }] in this order: outside_hours (at, as a minute of the UTC day, is in none of the hours; of null), then per range in the fence's order unread (no reading of that name that is an amount in the range's unit) or out_of_range (below min or above max); junk (of null) alone when the fence cannot be read, whatever its other fields. alone: heard is a time and at is no later than alone_until. alone_until: heard plus work_alone (PT0S when left out), null when heard is null. Hours and ranges left out fence nothing; silence about a reading never counts as inside

args: now?: the reader's clock, for a stop's scope.until (null reads none that needs a clock)
machine_lock.result: a reading (patterns/machines.md, A machine lock): { locked, locks, claimed }. locks: the ids of the standing stops of the machine (grants of kind stop, refs.subject the machine, counted, not ended) backed by the machine's owner as the ownership fold reads him in the stop's causal past (his own block, or one under a grant of his), sorted; claimed: the other standing stops of it, sorted, each its signer's reading; locked: locks is not empty

args: scope?: a grant's state.scope, or null (read as an empty scope)
scope_reading.result: { types, parties, on, limit, each, every, expires, clocks, deadline, fallback, junk }: the one reading of a scope, as authority.md reads its silence, and nothing filled in. types, parties and on: the lists as signed, [] when left out (no binding block named); limit and each: the amount, null when left out (no block under it draws above zero); every: a duration, null when left out; expires: a time, null when left out (it lasts until an end reaches it); clocks: { names, needed } as signed, null when left out (no clock named); deadline: a time, null when left out; fallback: lowest, null when left out; junk: the sorted names of the fields that are there but cannot be read (what the write check refuses in a scope, and any name that is no scope field; a scope that is no object is ["scope"]). An unreadable field reads as null or [] in the other keys, so a non-empty junk means the grant is held to no word

base_fields.result: the base fields of that type, beside `every`: the list in `fields`, or none for an open type

args: lookup: an observe of kind lookup
listing: an observe of kind listing
listing_check.result: promises.md, Finding: { ok, why, bad: [{ hash, why }], left_out: [hash] }. ok when every block the listing names in derives_from is, among the blocks, a real signed offer (or want, by the lookup's side) that the lookup asks for: a first promise, backed by its signing side, the other side open, still offered or asked, with a line naming one of the lookup's refs.what and carrying each of its terms. left_out: blocks given that fit the lookup and the listing does not name

args: check: an observe of kind check
check_reads.result: promises.md, A signed check: { ok, why, read: [{ hash, has, concerns, stage }] }. ok when every block the check names in derives_from is among the blocks and concerns refs.subject (they signed it or are a side of it) and each typed claim it makes holds: count (how many it names), of (the type of each), stage (the stage of each, a first promise)

args: clearing: an observe of kind clearing
clearing_applied.result: promises.md, Clearing: { binds, why, who, missing, lines: [{ deal, ok, why, to_come, reduce, left }] }. binds when every line reduces a binding deal by no more than is still to come in the deal's own kind (another kind only by a rate both sides of that deal signed (an observe of kind `rate`), with applies exactly the rate's worth) and every person in it (each debtor, each holder of the receiving place) has signed the clearing or a block that confirms it, backed by them; to_come, reduce and left are amounts

args: offer: a judge's offer (a promise under the base schema judging)
fee_back.result: promises.md, Rulings: { settled, releases, to_come, why }. settled when each side of the deal has signed a release of it (an observe of kind release, refs.subject the deal) that has no ruling of the judge's on the deal in its causal past; releases are those two blocks, sorted. to_come is [{ to, amount, returned, left }], one line per payer and kind, sorted, exact (no rounding): amount is the fee that payer paid (counted transfers to the judge, for the offer, refs.subject the deal) times the offer's terms.fee_back; returned what she has since sent that payer the same way; left the rest, never below zero. Empty unless the offer states terms.conciliation true and a fee_back and the sides settled

args: stake: a promise or a transfer
ruling_releases.result: promises.md, Rulings: { releases, to, amount, ruling, why }. The stake's condition (terms.condition of a promise, condition of a transfer) is { ruled, by, awards }. releases when the judge's head ruling on the deal, in the stake's relying block's past, awards that person something; amount is the award's, in the stake's own kind and capped at the stake (the whole stake when the award states none)

ruling_honoured.result: promises.md, Rulings: { lines: [{ to, due, honoured }], why }, a reading. One line per award of the ruling: honoured when counted transfers for the ruling to_owner the one it awards add up to its sum in its own kind, whoever paid, or when she released the ruling; an award with no sum only by her release. due is the award's own, or null; whether it was honoured by then is the reader's, against her own clock. A fact, never a verdict

live_keys.result: the keys of standing voices and keys under them that no standing key grant has ended, sorted (nodes.md, Messages)

add_duration.result: the time moved by the duration (sign 1 or -1), or null when either is not valid (core.md, section 3)

open_copy.result: open a sealed copy with the recipient's private encryption key: the block, its signature (the header's) and its reveals (privacy.md)

release_shown.result: { subject, released, kept_open }: who a release lets go of which claims, and the deals left open (promises.md)

circle_key.result: { epoch, keys, grants }: a circle's encryption key now, from the key grants signed as the circle for which a row holds, or every owner signed them (profiles/rekeys.md)

args: request: { since, limit, filter, heads, log?, seen? }
pull_request.result: a pull as an object { since, limit, filter, heads, log, seen } (nodes.md, Pull)

args: parts: { receipt?, had?, taken, unjudged, refused, unread, equivocations }, each list sorted as messages.push_answer_order says
push_answer.result: a node's signed answer to a push { node, receipt, taken, had, unjudged, refused, unread, equivocations, signature } (nodes.md, Messages)

args: receipts: [full_block]: the log's blocks, opened (a receipt given as only its header names nothing)
log_shown.result: { left_out: [id] ascending, stopped_short: boolean } (nodes.md, The arrival log): from receipts valid with `blocks` and on the request's log, and an answer that names the request's hash and log and is signed by a key that speaks for its node (else nothing is shown). Two logs is fork_pairs

args: document: { format, messages }, her export (nodes.md, A host), the log's receipts opened
log: id, the block that brought the log's key in
last: id, the block of the log she holds (a receipt or a dropped)
export_whole.result: { whole, lacks } (nodes.md, A host, Her record at a host): `whole` when `lacks` is empty. `lacks`, each once, the ids ascending, then each { author, key, seq } in the order of author, key (null first) and seq: what read_whole(last, log) lacks among the document's blocks (`last` not in it: its id); each block a receipt on the log names that is not in it, unless a dropped on the log names it or its receipt; each piece of a block in it that is not in it; and each block a receipt on the log names that is not in it and that a line a fold reads of a block in it lacks, read back from that block to the fold's own start. A `last` that is no block on the log is an argument error

waited_too_long.result: true when a waiting block has waited past the node's own time to live since it arrived

why_not_under.result: authority.md, A tool's word: [] where the block speaks for the grant's giver, else [{ code, detail }] with what the code carries: why (not_kept, the first sorted path of Keeps to that differs), pair (the fork answer { pair: true, blocks, at_most }), lacks (not_shown), waiting ([{ block, on }])

binds.result: true or false (1.9 stage 6, the owner's decision): whether the draft, signed, would bind anyone. True where it is an accept (state.status accepted), or where something of the one whose word it is would move (`gives` of that one, refs.as where it is signed as a circle, else refs.author, is not empty); else false. One rule, read from typed terms and refs only.

args: files: { <path under spec/>: <the file's bytes as text> }
rule_set.result: library (core.md, section 11): { id, manifest }. manifest is { files: { path: SHA-256 of the file's bytes } } over exactly the paths given; id is the SHA-256, in lowercase hex, of the manifest's canonical bytes

mount.result: library (core.md, section 12): a mount, 32 lowercase hex characters naming, for this door only, the set of blocks given so far; with `into`, the blocks are added to that mount's set and the same mount is returned. Every op that takes `blocks` takes a mount in its place and answers exactly as it does given the mount's set

unmount.result: true; the mount is forgotten, and a later op naming it is an argument error (unknown_mount)

args: block: the block a read-back is for, or its id among blocks
to?: the id of the person it is read back to (the readback's refs.to)
digits?: the digits the text ends in (text of digits, or a whole number)
readback.result: a reading (spec/readings/readback.md; profiles/short-form.md, A read-back that can be redone): { answer, text, state }. answer is readings/readback's (its `read`, the sorted ids it read, and `lacks`); text is the renderer's words over the answer, one space, the digits (the words alone where no digits are given); state is exactly the state of the observe an honest host signs: { kind: readback, readback: the SHA-256 hex of text's UTF-8 bytes, reading, renderer: each named as a rule set is, the hash of the manifest over its published text and its cases, read: the answer's read, digits }; for en-sms also texts: the text, whole and in order, over texts of at most 160 characters split at spaces (spec/renderers/en-sms.md, Texts)

args: rb: an observe of kind readback, its state { readback, reading, renderer, read, digits } and refs.for, refs.to
readback_redo.result: a reading: { same, readback, lacks, not_run }, run on the ids of state.read (and refs.for) alone, read to refs.to: same true where the digest made is state.readback, else false; an input not among the blocks: same and readback null, lacks those ids, sorted; a reading or renderer this build does not run: same and readback null, not_run those names

render.result: a renderer (spec/renderers/en.md, en-sms.md): the words in that language, from the answer only (never a block; free text never read, the deal's own words quoted word for word)

door.classes_about: Every op of `ops` outside `protocol`, sorted (changes-1.9/07-last.md D2): a reading (computed from blocks; changes none of the four answers), library (a tool or data), or a node's own business.

conventions.block: { type, state, refs }: a block as written (core.md, section 1).
conventions.full_block: a block with its `hash` (its id), its `signature` (hex) and, when its key's suite is not std, `suite`: { hash, type, state, refs, signature, suite? }. This is what an op that takes blocks given, a story or a store reads. Order in a list of blocks never matters.
conventions.id: a hash: 64 lowercase hex (or a hash name and colon first). `time`: the text of core.md, section 3. `clock` or `now`: a time; anything else (other than null where the clock may be left out) is an argument error, never read as a time. A list argument (written `[...]` in an op's args) given as anything but a list, or null, is an argument error, never read as the empty list.
conventions.text: every argument is JSON as I-JSON (RFC 7493) writes it: a string holding a lone surrogate is no text, and an argument error. Bytes that are not well-formed reach a reader only as bytes, and are not_canonical (canonical.md).
conventions.refusals: a list of { code, detail }. A case with `codes` compares the codes only, in the order of protocol.json refusals.codes. Details are free text.
conventions.keys: public keys and signatures are hex as in core.md, section 2; a private key is the seed hex for p256 and sm, and for std the seed, which `keypair` also writes as PKCS#8 DER hex (`302e020100300506032b657004220420` then the 32 seed bytes).
conventions.suite_arg: an optional suite name, default std
